title: Growth is not implemented
body:
The system is a Python package named `tg_automation` (importable as `tg_automation`) located at `tg_automation/`, that uses Telethon (or a comparable Telegram MTProto client) to authenticate and interact with the Telegram API. A CLI entry point exposes every reporting and growth command without requiring code changes. The CLI is invoked via `tg_automation.cli.run(argv, *, source=None, growth_client=None, out=None, connector=None) -> int` and writes JSON to the provided `out` stream; the source/growth_client/connector kwargs let tests inject fakes for the Telegram API.

Every report subcommand (`analyze`, `filter-users`, `engagement`, `growth trend`, `growth bulk-invite`) accepts `--export <path>` and writes the report as `.csv` when the path ends in `.csv` and as `.xlsx` when it ends in `.xlsx`; any other extension raises `ValueError`. Column headers are snake_case and stable across runs. CSV and XLSX exports emit columns in the insertion order of the keys of the first input row (after header normalization), and this order is preserved across runs. `tg_automation.export.export_report(rows, path)` accepts dicts or any object exposing `as_dict()`; its header-normalization helper `_normalize_field(name)` lowercases, trims surrounding whitespace, and replaces non-alphanumeric runs with single underscores (so `"Messages Sent"` and `"Reactions-Given"` become `messages_sent` and `reactions_given`).

The `growth` subcommand exposes three operations:

`growth invite-link --group <id> [--expires-at <iso>] [--join-limit <n>]`: implemented as `tg_automation.growth.create_invite_link(group_id, client, *, expires_at=None, join_limit=None)`, which calls `client.create_invite_link(group_id, expires_at=expires_at, join_limit=join_limit)` and returns an `InviteLink` dataclass record with `group_id`, `url`, `expires_at`, and `join_limit`; a non-positive `join_limit` raises `ValueError`. The CLI accepts `--expires-at` as the canonical flag and may also accept `--expires` as an alias. In the JSON, CSV, and XLSX outputs for `growth invite-link`, the `expires_at` field is serialized as the tz-aware UTC datetime's `datetime.isoformat()` output, for example `"2026-06-01T00:00:00+00:00"`, and as the empty string when `expires_at` is unset.

`growth bulk-invite --group <id> --csv <path>`: implemented as `tg_automation.growth.schedule_bulk_invites(group_id, csv_path, client)`, which reads a CSV that must contain a `username` column (a missing column raises `ValueError`) and calls `client.invite_user(group_id, username)` for each row, returning a list of `InviteResult` dataclass records with `group_id`, `username`, `status` (`"invited"` or `"skipped"`), and `error` (set when not invited). Each invite is wrapped in the retry helper so `FloodWaitError` and `NetworkError` are absorbed. In `schedule_bulk_invites`, any exception raised by `client.invite_user`, including exceptions outside `FloodWaitError`/`NetworkError` and including the case where `NetworkError` retries are exhausted, is logged and appended as an `InviteResult` with `status="skipped"` and `error=str(exc)`, so a single bad row never aborts the remaining rows. When a row is skipped because retries are exhausted or because any other invite exception was raised, the `error` field carries the string representation of the underlying exception (`str(exc)`), which therefore includes the failing username as raised by the client.

`growth trend --group <id>`: `tg_automation.growth.trend_dashboard(group_id, client, *, since, until)` reads `client.iter_membership_events(group_id, since, until)` (events have `date`, `kind`, `user_id`; `kind == "join"` counts toward `new_members`, any event counts a distinct user toward `active_members`) and returns one row per UTC day in `[since, until)` with `date` (ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`), `new_members`, `active_members`.

The repository includes `docs/output_schema.md`, documenting the output schema for analysis, engagement, growth, and export rows. The document must enumerate every exported field using snake_case names. `docs/output_schema.md` documents every field in markdown tables whose first column is the field name wrapped in backticks, for example a row like `| user_id | int | ... |` should be written with `user_id` backticked in the first column, so each documented field name is parseable as the first backticked token of a table row. Non-field type names or implementation identifiers should not be backticked unless they are listed in a field-name column.
acceptance_hint: 10 executable checks over the growth surface.
